name: Eastern Hongshuihe Zhuang
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: van de Weijer, Jeroen, Yuhan Lin & Weiyun Wei. 2025. Hongshui He Zhuang (Baima dialect). Journal of the International Phonetic Association 55, 537-555 (Illustration of the IPA, open access). doi:10.1017/S0025100325100704
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent. 'Prosodic features' (pp. 550-552) treats only tone: 'Zhuang is a tone language.. In the Hongshui He (Baima) dialect, there are also eight phonemic tones' + tone table and f0 contours; 'Syllable structure' (C)(G)V(C). No word on stress/accent/rhythm (a full-text search for stress/accent found nothing). Speaker from Baima Town, Hechi City (phonology based on Zhang et al. 1999's Du'an point); authors tag it 'Glottolog: east2363' but also 'ISO 639-3: zch' -- geographically the zch/cent2009 area.

sources.citation: Liao, Zhi-En, K. Ganesan & Jane Wong Kon Ling. 2024. Differences between English and the Zhuang language in phoneme and word stress. Higher Education and Practice 1(7). doi:10.62381/h241701
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Not this language (Standard/Wuming-based Zhuang) and not usable: 'word stress of Standard Zhuang is manifested by its tone' (sec. 4.3, 5.2) -- conflates stress with tone, gives no stress position.

sources.citation: Ethnologue 17th ed. (2014) entry 'Zhuang, Eastern Hongshuihe [zeh]' (Internet Archive copy 2014-09-25).

sources.citation: Castro, Andy & Bruce Hansen. 2010. Hongshui He Zhuang dialect intelligibility survey. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2010-025. Dallas: SIL International. 110 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent. Sec. 5.2 tone analysis and App. I/K tone values for the Hongshui He data points (incl. Guigang, Guiping, Wuxuan, Xingbin, Shanglin); App. E 'Zhuang syllable structure for all varieties surveyed is (C)V(C)', 'monosyllabic words dominate'. a full-text search for stress/accent/unstress/prominence: 0 hits. Only SIL/OLAC item for zeh.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2007. Change Request 2007-027 (Sharon Tan) + Request for New Language Code Element zeh and zch.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; identity/location only (zeh = S Shanglin, S Xincheng, S Xingbin, N Guigang, W Guiping, S Wuxuan; zch = Du'an, Dahua, Mashan, N Shanglin).

sources.note: The standard dialectology of Zhuang with full phonologies of Hongshui He survey points inside the zeh area (来宾 Laibin, 贵港 Guigang, 上林 Shanglin) plus a general phonology chapter; the most likely place for any remark on 轻声/重音 in these varieties, and the base description the JIPA authors adapted.
